## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly matches the validated locator [source-6@L14-L16|claim=ordinary-document]. It supports only the historical conjecture, not minimality itself.
- claim-2: The calculation is correct under the stated integral box/Schur/Pieri hypotheses. For \(p=1\), \(u\) is outside the box; for \(c\ge2\), \(w\) remains. The complementary minor has determinant \(-1\), so the degree-\(d+2\) quotient is integrally free on \(\bar x_2\), with \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\); degree \(d+1\) similarly gives \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\). Completeness of the displayed rows requires the homogeneous-component argument: \(J_{<d}=0\), \((A_+J)_{d+1}=A_1J_d\), and \((A_+J)_{d+2}=A_2J_d+A_1J_{d+1}\). This is available in accepted project context but should be stated rather than hidden in “complete Pieri rows.” No higher-degree conclusion follows.
- claim-3: Correct. For example, adjoining a summand \(\mathbb Z\) in degree \(d+3\), with \(A\) acting through \(A/A_+\cong\mathbb Z\), preserves all computed components through degree \(d+2\). Thus the certificate cannot prove \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\).

## Required revisions
- Clarify that claim-2 concerns precisely the graded truncation \(Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2}\), not all of \(Q\).
- Include the componentwise row-completeness argument, including the integral spanning of \(A_2\) and the redundancy \(h_1^2x_0=h_1x_1+h_1y_1\).
- Retain the opposite boundary case and the all-degree graded-kernel/saturation argument as separate unresolved follow-on tasks. Do not infer generation, minimality, or the parent theorem from this certificate.
